newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina proposes leaner public administration.
newsitem.headline: Argentina proposes leaner public administration.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem announced Tuesday a project to decentralize the government and help eliminate redundancies between the federal administration and the provinces.
The initiative, called the "New Federalism" project, will seek to divide the country in six regions, resulting in smaller bureaucracies and streamlined operations, Menem said.
It would also detect areas where the central administration and the provinces duplicate activities.
"In 10 days we will send the project to the Senate, because that is where the provinces are better represented," Menem told a press conference.
He said the plan is important "because budgetary and fiscal constraints are forcing us to rationalize public spending."
The government is now trying to pass through Congress a tax package to help reduce a fiscal deficit that could reach $6.6 billion this year, according to official estimates.
